req.title: Status code sentence body
req.statement: The system shall include the standard reason phrase in the body when responding to /status/<code> with a code between 400 and 599.

doc.reasoning: R-HTTPBIN-045 requires that GET /status/<code> for codes 400-599 returns a response whose body contains the standard HTTP reason phrase. The status_code() helper in helpers.py builds the response via make_response() and sets r.status_code; for most codes in 400-599 the body is empty (no entry in code_map), so the reason phrase must come from Flask/Werkzeug's default status line or body. Examining the actual httpbin behaviour: the endpoint returns the status code itself as the HTTP status, and the body contains the reason phrase as plain text (e.g. b'BAD REQUEST' for 400). Tests must cover: (1) a representative 4xx code body contains the phrase (EP/positive), (2) a representative 5xx code body contains the phrase (EP/positive), (3) the boundary at 400 (BVA - first code in range), (4) the boundary at 599 (BVA - last code in range), (5) code 399 is outside range and should not be treated as a 4xx error phrase case (BVA/NEG), (6) code 600 is outside range (BVA/NEG), (7) a special-cased code like 402 whose body is overridden (DT), (8) a 5xx code like 500 (EP). We assert exact status codes and exact body content to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_status_400_body_contains_reason_phrase
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
GET /status/400 is a valid endpoint
expected: HTTP response status code is exactly 400
Response body contains 'BAD REQUEST' (case-insensitive)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-045: 400 is in [400,599]; body must contain standard reason phrase 'Bad Request'
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_status_400_body_contains_reason_phrase():
    r = client.get('/status/400')
    assert r.status_code == 400
    body = r.data.decode('utf-8', errors='replace').upper()
    assert 'BAD REQUEST' in body

tests.name: test_status_boundary_401_vs_400_distinct
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
400 and 401 are adjacent codes with different reason phrases
expected: GET /status/400 returns status 400 with body containing 'BAD REQUEST'
GET /status/401 returns status 401 with body containing 'UNAUTHORIZED'
Bodies are distinct from each other
trace: R-HTTPBIN-045: BVA adjacent boundary; each code must return its own distinct reason phrase
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_status_boundary_401_vs_400_distinct():
    r400 = client.get('/status/400')
    assert r400.status_code == 400
    body400 = r400.data.decode('utf-8', errors='replace').upper()
    assert 'BAD REQUEST' in body400
    r401 = client.get('/status/401')
    assert r401.status_code == 401
    body401 = r401.data.decode('utf-8', errors='replace').upper()
    assert 'UNAUTHORIZED' in body401
    assert body400 != body401
